title: A thread is a worker
sub: Threads, cores and the OS scheduler
cards/0/body:
A thread is a worker that walks through code line by line. Every program has at least one, the main thread.

You can create more threads, and they will run at the same time: on different CPU cores, or taking turns on one.
cards/1/body:
Threads are managed by the OS scheduler. It lets a thread run for a short time slice and can switch to another at any moment, even in the middle of a line of code.

Picture two cooks in one kitchen: the head chef decides who does what, and can interrupt either of them mid-sentence.
cards/1/deep: A time slice is on the order of tens of milliseconds; a context switch costs microseconds. On a machine with N cores, at most N threads truly run at once.
cards/2/explain: After Start(), the two threads run independently. The output order can change from run to run.
cards/3/task: You are the scheduler. Two threads do count++, and you decide whose step is next. Run both threads to completion.
cards/4/q: What is true about threads? Select all that apply.
cards/4/options/0: Each thread has its own stack
cards/4/options/1: The heap is shared by all threads
cards/4/options/2: The scheduler can interrupt a thread at any moment
cards/4/options/3: Threads run strictly in the order they were created
cards/4/explain: Separate stacks and a shared heap follow straight from the memory unit. Extra threads just get in each other's way.
cards/5/q: How expensive is creating a thread?
cards/5/options/0: Noticeably: stack memory plus OS work, which is why threads get reused
cards/5/explain: Each thread needs its own stack, typically around a megabyte of address space, plus system structures. That's why the thread pool exists (lesson 4).
cards/6/title: A shared heap is a source of trouble
cards/6/body:
Each thread has its own local variables: they live on its stack. But objects on the heap are shared.

If two threads change the same object at once, the result can break. How exactly is the next lesson.
cards/7/q: Two threads run the same method with a local variable int i. How many i variables are there?
cards/7/options/0: Two: each thread has its own stack and its own frame
cards/7/explain: Every method call gets its own frame on its own thread's stack.
cards/8/pairs/0/1: A worker that walks through code
